[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Omadacycline, a modern tetracycline with a polar C9 basic side chain, has measured absolute oral bioavailability of 34.5% in healthy adults after a 300 mg fasted standard tablet, 31.2% in CF patients, and 31% in monkeys, all above the 20% threshold.

Tetracycline has human oral bioavailability reported as 75%, >70%, and 80–90%, and L3 oral exposure records show substantial absorption (500 mg tetracycline alone: geometric mean Cmax 4.57 µg/mL and AUC0-∞ 67.4 µg·h/mL), supporting that the tetracycline core can achieve F≥20% in humans.
L5 doxycycline Caco-2 records show A-B Papp of 3.4 ± 0.23 ×10^-6 cm/s and an efflux ratio of 1.2, indicating that the tetracycline class can exhibit good permeability and minimal P-gp efflux.

L6 hepatic-clearance records for tetracycline-class molecules show low metabolic clearance: doxycycline HLM CLint <7 µL/min/mg, minocycline predicted in vivo hepatic metabolic clearance 0.87 ml/min/kg (~4.2% of hepatic blood flow), COL-3 low hepatic extraction, and tigecycline HLM CLint 6.3 µL/min/mg; this reduces concern that first-pass hepatic metabolism would drive F below 20%.

Class-level gut-wall concerns (tetracycline P-gp substrate, mucin barrier) and species/formulation-specific low values (omadacycline slow-dissolution tablet 0.5%, rodent lack of oral bioavailability, rat in situ absorption 4.8%) are not affirmative evidence of F<20% for the query in a human standard-oral context, because tetracycline itself has high human F and doxycycline shows low efflux.

evidence_gaps: No direct eravacycline-specific absolute oral bioavailability, permeability, efflux, or hepatic-clearance record is present; the decision relies on transfer from omadacycline, tetracycline, doxycycline, minocycline, and tigecycline clearance.

Target species is not explicitly specified; omadacycline lacks oral bioavailability in rodents (C108) and tetracycline rat in situ absorption is low (C220), so a rodent-based endpoint would substantially weaken the high prediction.
Formulation and prandial conditions for the query are unspecified; omadacycline F ranges from 0.5% for a slow-dissolution tablet to 34.5% for a standard fasted tablet (C49, C18).

Tigecycline, a structurally related glycylcycline, appears only in L6 clearance records; its oral bioavailability is not supplied, and C334 indicates predominant biliary excretion and glucuronidation, so its transferability as a negative/positive class example is unresolved.
Many L6 records are for unrelated molecules (tivantinib, anthracyclines, fluoroquinolones, etc.) and were not used as evidence for the query.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
